items.title: Ask this book feature now on Kindle ereaders
items.excerpt: Kindle Software Update 5.20.2 brings the AI-powered "Ask This Book" feature directly to Kindle e-readers.
items.rationale: A new release: Kindle firmware 5.20.2 puts the AI 'Ask This Book' Q&A on e-reader hardware, which changes the reading experience for a large installed base. The LibreOffice and Kindle Plus stories in the history are different products.

items.title: In Letter to the Court, Textbook Authors Complain of Unfair Process, Splits in Anthropic Settlement
items.excerpt: Amid a growing number of disputes, TAA Executive Director Kim Pawlak asked the court to "consider and acknowledge the inherent burden on authors" in the $1.5 billion settlement claims process compared to the better-resourced publishers.
items.rationale: Follow-up on the Anthropic settlement with a new filing: the Textbook & Academic Authors Association sent the court a letter about the author/publisher claims process and payout splits. It bears directly on authors' payouts and is a separate action from the Stanford opt-out suit published 10-30.

items.title: Gemini Notebook makes hundreds of textbooks available to help students learn even more
items.excerpt: Add textbooks from OpenStax and S Chand to Google Gemini Notebook. Generate custom study guides and quizzes now. See the available catalog.
items.rationale: A primary-source product launch: licensed OpenStax and S Chand textbooks can now be loaded into Gemini Notebook to make study guides and quizzes. It is a new publisher-content deal for an AI product and is distinct from the Play Books Expert Intelligence story of 10-17.

items.title: 'Two-headed shrimp' error in AI-generated illustrations prompts recall of marine life books in China
items.excerpt: China Agricultural Publishing House is recalling a popular-science series on South China Sea marine life after readers spotted an AI-generated 'two-headed shrimp'; the books' preface said most illustrations were made with AI tools.
items.rationale: A concrete new event: a state publisher recalled a printed nonfiction series because of an AI illustration error. It is a clear warning about AI art QA in publishing, and no earlier recall from this publisher has run.

items.title: 출협 "말뭉치 사업 합의금액, AI 학습용 데이터 표준 대가 될 수 없다"
items.excerpt: 사단법인 대한출판문화협회(이하 출협)가 최근 대법원 상고심이 진행 중인 국립국어원 말뭉치 사건과 관련해 과거 분쟁 해결 차원의 합의 금액이 향후 AI 학습용 데이터
items.rationale: A new official statement from the Korean Publishers Association: as the National Institute of Korean Language corpus case reaches the Supreme Court, it says the old settlement amount must not become the price benchmark for AI training data. This is a distinct case from the 10-17 KPC compensation demand and the book-buying stories.

https://publishingperspectives.com/2026/.new_action: The Textbook & Academic Authors Association filed a letter with the court objecting to the author-vs-publisher claims process and payout splits in the $1.5B Anthropic settlement (a new court filing).
